# Local trajectory explorer

Python 3.10+ is required. Install the local dependencies once, then start the
indexer and web server with one command:

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m explorer
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. The process reads only local `export/*.jsonl` and
`results/*.jsonl` files. It makes no telemetry, analytics, CDN, font, or other
network requests.

For frontend development:

```bash
cd explorer/frontend
npm install
npm run build
```

The production bundle is committed under `explorer/static/`, so Node is not
needed to run the explorer. Dataset rows are never included in that bundle.

## What the tabs show

| Tab | What it answers |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | What the corpus costs, which models spend it, how much of it is the uncached cold start, and how concentrated it is. Also states plainly whether `results/*.jsonl` joined. |
| **Classes** | Ten ways the inputs sort themselves — workload, trigger, harness, chat surface, toolset, size, depth, cron family, loop shape, model. All read out of the requests, none guessed. Click a row to filter the trajectory list. |
| **Function calls** | Each tool ranked by the tokens its *result* adds to every later prompt — i.e. which calls make a run expensive to continue, not which are called most. |
| **Trajectories** | Faceted list of runs. Open one for its Flow: call by call, each request a bar split cached / new / output, with per-call cost, tool chips and expandable item text. |
| **Compare** | Nearest runs by tool overlap and loop shape, then an LCS alignment of two runs showing which steps both took and where the cost gap sits. Plus matched cohorts as an off-policy estimate, with the size-spread confounder exposed. |
| **Files** | `export/` and `results/` line by line: what each file contributed, each row's decomposition, and the raw JSON. Jump from a raw line to its Flow. |
| **Raw calls** | The unopinionated 50-column table over the `calls` index. |

## Reading the numbers

Every table header carries its own definition: hover (or tab to) a column name for a
note saying what the number is and where it can be wrong. The Raw calls tab reads its
columns off the DuckDB schema, so its notes ride on the native tooltip. All of that
text lives in one place, `explorer/frontend/src/glossary.ts`.

Every token count is an **estimate** — serialized JSON chars / 4. The export ships no
`usage` field, so nothing here is measured. Outputs are recovered from the next call's
input, which leaves the final turn of every trajectory unobservable. Costs are
cache-aware and input+output, at the official rates in `scripts/cost_model.py`.

One export line is one **complete trajectory**, not one call: the agent loop ran inside
it, and `scripts/decompose.py` unfolds it into the ~10.8k requests that actually ran.
Trajectory ids are that decomposition's ids. A router artifact in `results/` only shows
up in the cost columns if its ids were minted the same way — the Overview tab reports
whether they were.
{
  "name": "viktor-trajectory-explorer",
  "private": true,
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc -b && vite build",
    "dev": "vite"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@tanstack/react-table": "^8.21.3",
    "@tanstack/react-virtual": "^3.13.12",
    "react": "^19.1.1",
    "react-dom": "^19.1.1"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/react": "^19.1.10",
    "@types/react-dom": "^19.1.7",
    "@vitejs/plugin-react": "^5.0.2",
    "typescript": "^5.9.2",
    "vite": "^7.1.3"
  }
}
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  base: "/",
  build: {
    outDir: "../static",
    emptyOutDir: true,
    sourcemap: false,
  },
  server: {
    proxy: { "/api": "http://127.0.0.1:8000" },
  },
});

# Local trajectory explorer

Python 3.10+ is required. Install the local dependencies once, then start the
indexer and web server with one command:

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m explorer
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. The process reads only local `export/*.jsonl` and
`results/*.jsonl` files. It makes no telemetry, analytics, CDN, font, or other
network requests.

For frontend development:

```bash
cd explorer/frontend
npm install
npm run build
```

The production bundle is committed under `explorer/static/`, so Node is not
needed to run the explorer. Dataset rows are never included in that bundle.

## What the tabs show

| Tab | What it answers |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | What the corpus costs, which models spend it, how much of it is the uncached cold start, and how concentrated it is. Also states plainly whether `results/*.jsonl` joined. |
| **Classes** | Ten ways the inputs sort themselves — workload, trigger, harness, chat surface, toolset, size, depth, cron family, loop shape, model. All read out of the requests, none guessed. Click a row to filter the trajectory list. |
| **Function calls** | Each tool ranked by the tokens its *result* adds to every later prompt — i.e. which calls make a run expensive to continue, not which are called most. |
| **Trajectories** | Faceted list of runs. Open one for its Flow: call by call, each request a bar split cached / new / output, with per-call cost, tool chips and expandable item text. |
| **Compare** | Nearest runs by tool overlap and loop shape, then an LCS alignment of two runs showing which steps both took and where the cost gap sits. Plus matched cohorts as an off-policy estimate, with the size-spread confounder exposed. |
| **Files** | `export/` and `results/` line by line: what each file contributed, each row's decomposition, and the raw JSON. Jump from a raw line to its Flow. |
| **Raw calls** | The unopinionated 50-column table over the `calls` index. |

## Reading the numbers

Every table header carries its own definition: hover (or tab to) a column name for a
note saying what the number is and where it can be wrong. The Raw calls tab reads its
columns off the DuckDB schema, so its notes ride on the native tooltip. All of that
text lives in one place, `explorer/frontend/src/glossary.ts`.

Every token count is an **estimate** — serialized JSON chars / 4. The export ships no
`usage` field, so nothing here is measured. Outputs are recovered from the next call's
input, which leaves the final turn of every trajectory unobservable. Costs are
cache-aware and input+output, at the official rates in `scripts/cost_model.py`.

One export line is one **complete trajectory**, not one call: the agent loop ran inside
it, and `scripts/decompose.py` unfolds it into the ~10.8k requests that actually ran.
Trajectory ids are that decomposition's ids. A router artifact in `results/` only shows
up in the cost columns if its ids were minted the same way — the Overview tab reports
whether they were.

name: Deploy Routemaxxing demo to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, routemaxing]
    paths:
      - docs/**
      - .github/workflows/pages.yml
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - name: Upload static demo
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: docs
      - name: Deploy GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DOCS = ROOT / "docs"


def demo_data():
    source = (DOCS / "data.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    match = re.fullmatch(r"window\.ROUTEMAXXING_DEMO = (.*);\n", source, re.S)
    assert match
    return json.loads(match.group(1))


def test_static_demo_has_no_absolute_asset_paths_and_all_assets_exist():
    html = (DOCS / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assets = re.findall(r'(?:href|src)="(\./[^"]+)"', html)
    assert {"./styles.css", "./data.js", "./app.js"} <= set(assets)
    assert all((DOCS / asset[2:]).is_file() for asset in assets)
    assert 'href="/' not in html
    assert 'src="/' not in html


def test_demo_data_is_aggregate_only_and_matches_locked_headline():
    data = demo_data()
    encoded = json.dumps(data)
    assert data["headline"]["routed_cost"] == 48.1798
    assert data["headline"]["savings_pct"] == 45.79
    assert data["headline"]["failure_upper95_pp"] <= 2.0
    assert data["support"]["gpt-5.6-luna"]["eligible"] is False
    assert "trajectory_id" not in encoded
    assert "opening_user" not in encoded
    assert "<PERSON" not in encoded


def test_certified_demo_routes_preserve_family_and_never_upgrade():
    data = demo_data()
    pricing = data["pricing"]
    for default, selected in data["certified_downgrades"].items():
        assert default.split("-")[0] == selected.split("-")[0]
        assert all(a <= b for a, b in zip(pricing[selected], pricing[default]))


def test_pages_workflow_deploys_docs_directory():
    workflow = (ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "pages.yml").read_text()
    assert "actions/configure-pages@v5" in workflow
    assert "actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4" in workflow
    assert "actions/deploy-pages@v4" in workflow
    assert "path: docs" in workflow

        "message": "Update portfolio from new CV and add three.js scenes\n\nContent now mirrors Utku_Kalkanli_CV.pdf:\n- About rewritten around computer vision / MLOps / agentic AI; stats are\n  now mAP 80->95%, ETL -37.5%, 91% radar accuracy, 1 patented invention\n- Skills restructured into the CV's six groups, adding 3D Vision and\n  NLP & LLMs; earlier Gaussian Splatting / NeRF / ICP work retained\n- Fraunhofer: zero-shot detection on CLIP/DINOv2/VGGT, VLM explainability,\n  LangGraph agentic framework, CAD-to-mesh, 3DV/ICRA manuscripts\n- Linde GmbH (was AG): AIRGENIOUS Azure ML 8h->5h, MDR certification,\n  RF-DETR on satellite imagery, named inventor of invention P40700\n- Education: TUM Apr 2023 - Oct 2026 with new minors and thesis line;\n  Bilkent from Sep 2017, GPA dropped\n- Contact: CV download in hero and footer, German at B1\n- Dropped the expired Google TensorFlow certificate\n\nAdd three WebGL scenes in three-scenes.js (three.js r160 via import map):\n- Hero point cloud with a shader-driven scan sweep and mouse parallax\n- Skills tag sphere via CSS3DRenderer, behind a Grid/Sphere toggle\n- Interactive scan-vs-CAD anomaly detection demo with a deviation heat map\n\nAll three are progressive enhancement: with the CDN blocked or WebGL\nmissing, the 2D particle background keeps running, the demo falls back to\nexplanatory text, and the skills grid stays the default view.\n\nRewrite CLAUDE.md to describe this repo (static GitHub Pages site) instead\nof an unrelated Spring Boot/React project.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED",

        "message": "Update portfolio from new CV and add three.js scenes\n\nContent now mirrors Utku_Kalkanli_CV.pdf:\n- About rewritten around computer vision / MLOps / agentic AI; stats are\n  now mAP 80->95%, ETL -37.5%, 91% radar accuracy, 1 patented invention\n- Skills restructured into the CV's six groups, adding 3D Vision and\n  NLP & LLMs; earlier Gaussian Splatting / NeRF / ICP work retained\n- Fraunhofer: zero-shot detection on CLIP/DINOv2/VGGT, VLM explainability,\n  LangGraph agentic framework, CAD-to-mesh, 3DV/ICRA manuscripts\n- Linde GmbH (was AG): AIRGENIOUS Azure ML 8h->5h, MDR certification,\n  RF-DETR on satellite imagery, named inventor of invention P40700\n- Education: TUM Apr 2023 - Oct 2026 with new minors and thesis line;\n  Bilkent from Sep 2017, GPA dropped\n- Contact: CV download in hero and footer, German at B1\n- Dropped the expired Google TensorFlow certificate\n\nAdd three WebGL scenes in three-scenes.js (three.js r160 via import map):\n- Hero point cloud with a shader-driven scan sweep and mouse parallax\n- Skills tag sphere via CSS3DRenderer, behind a Grid/Sphere toggle\n- Interactive scan-vs-CAD anomaly detection demo with a deviation heat map\n\nAll three are progressive enhancement: with the CDN blocked or WebGL\nmissing, the 2D particle background keeps running, the demo falls back to\nexplanatory text, and the skills grid stays the default view.\n\nRewrite CLAUDE.md to describe this repo (static GitHub Pages site) instead\nof an unrelated Spring Boot/React project.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED",

        "message": "Update portfolio from new CV and add three.js scenes\n\nContent now mirrors Utku_Kalkanli_CV.pdf:\n- About rewritten around computer vision / MLOps / agentic AI; stats are\n  now mAP 80->95%, ETL -37.5%, 91% radar accuracy, 1 patented invention\n- Skills restructured into the CV's six groups, adding 3D Vision and\n  NLP & LLMs; earlier Gaussian Splatting / NeRF / ICP work retained\n- Fraunhofer: zero-shot detection on CLIP/DINOv2/VGGT, VLM explainability,\n  LangGraph agentic framework, CAD-to-mesh, 3DV/ICRA manuscripts\n- Linde GmbH (was AG): AIRGENIOUS Azure ML 8h->5h, MDR certification,\n  RF-DETR on satellite imagery, named inventor of invention P40700\n- Education: TUM Apr 2023 - Oct 2026 with new minors and thesis line;\n  Bilkent from Sep 2017, GPA dropped\n- Contact: CV download in hero and footer, German at B1\n- Dropped the expired Google TensorFlow certificate\n\nAdd three WebGL scenes in three-scenes.js (three.js r160 via import map):\n- Hero point cloud with a shader-driven scan sweep and mouse parallax\n- Skills tag sphere via CSS3DRenderer, behind a Grid/Sphere toggle\n- Interactive scan-vs-CAD anomaly detection demo with a deviation heat map\n\nAll three are progressive enhancement: with the CDN blocked or WebGL\nmissing, the 2D particle background keeps running, the demo falls back to\nexplanatory text, and the skills grid stays the default view.\n\nRewrite CLAUDE.md to describe this repo (static GitHub Pages site) instead\nof an unrelated Spring Boot/React project.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED",

        "message": "Update portfolio from new CV and add three.js scenes\n\nContent now mirrors Utku_Kalkanli_CV.pdf:\n- About rewritten around computer vision / MLOps / agentic AI; stats are\n  now mAP 80->95%, ETL -37.5%, 91% radar accuracy, 1 patented invention\n- Skills restructured into the CV's six groups, adding 3D Vision and\n  NLP & LLMs; earlier Gaussian Splatting / NeRF / ICP work retained\n- Fraunhofer: zero-shot detection on CLIP/DINOv2/VGGT, VLM explainability,\n  LangGraph agentic framework, CAD-to-mesh, 3DV/ICRA manuscripts\n- Linde GmbH (was AG): AIRGENIOUS Azure ML 8h->5h, MDR certification,\n  RF-DETR on satellite imagery, named inventor of invention P40700\n- Education: TUM Apr 2023 - Oct 2026 with new minors and thesis line;\n  Bilkent from Sep 2017, GPA dropped\n- Contact: CV download in hero and footer, German at B1\n- Dropped the expired Google TensorFlow certificate\n\nAdd three WebGL scenes in three-scenes.js (three.js r160 via import map):\n- Hero point cloud with a shader-driven scan sweep and mouse parallax\n- Skills tag sphere via CSS3DRenderer, behind a Grid/Sphere toggle\n- Interactive scan-vs-CAD anomaly detection demo with a deviation heat map\n\nAll three are progressive enhancement: with the CDN blocked or WebGL\nmissing, the 2D particle background keeps running, the demo falls back to\nexplanatory text, and the skills grid stays the default view.\n\nRewrite CLAUDE.md to describe this repo (static GitHub Pages site) instead\nof an unrelated Spring Boot/React project.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED",
